question.leadin: This person was given command of the 7th Panzer Division, which earned the nickname "Ghost Division" under his command.
question.text: Name this Nazi general who lead the North Africa Corps and was nicknamed the "Desert Fox"
question.clue: This man was allowed to commit suicide, rather than face trial, after being implicated in Claus von Stauffenberg's ("klaus von stow-fehn-behrg's") July 20th plot.

swap.leadin: This group was opposed by an organization called the Lizard League. which has nothing to do with any insane modern conspiracy theories.
swap.text: Name this Christian order of crusading knights, who converted the Baltic countries to Christianity. They were defeated by the forces of Wladyslaw II Jagiello (vwah-DEE-swahf "the second" yah-GYEH-woh) at the Battle of Grunwald.
swap.answerHtml: Teutonic Order [or the Teutonic Knights, or the Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem]
swap.clue: This group managed to defend its capital at Marienburg despite losing Grandmaster Ulrich von Jungingen in a defeat to Polish-Lithuanian forces at the Battle of Grunwald.

question.leadin: According to the Venerable Bede, they invaded Britannia together with the Angles and Jutes in the 5th century.
question.text: Name these people, the namesake of upper and lower regions in modern-day Germany.
question.clue: By then they would also divide into two groups, with the western one being founded by Cerdic, though it was Cerdic's grandson Egbert who was the first of them to be recognized as a great king.

swap.text: This Prussian leader and victor at Laon defeated Napoleon at Leipzig. He crushed Marmont's Sixth Corps and was promoted to Field Marshall after the battle.
swap.clue: Dismissed from his governorship of Pomerania in 1812 for his ardent support of another war, at Auerstadt, he repeatedly led unsuccessful cavalry charges, and refused to surrender with the rest of Hohenlohe's corps.

question.leadin: This entity waged war against Valdemar IV's Denmark in order to secure profits from Danish trade, accomplished in the Treaty of Stralsund.
question.text: Name this league of northern German states, a commercial confederation which dominated northern European sea trade.
question.clue: This group's trading post at Torun was founded by the Teutonic Knights, and members of the three Drittels in this polity elected aldermen to lead its independent trading outposts, called kontors.

swap.text: The content of the Ninety-five Theses was rapidly spread across Europe using the printing press, an invention of this former German goldsmith, a creator of a namesake version of the Bible, from his workshop in Mainz.
swap.clue: This man's invention of hand molds and an oil-based substance helped him create his most well-known invention.

question.leadin: Answer the following about captive hippopotami in history.
question.text: During this war, besieged Parisians took to eating zoo animals, although the asking price for hippo meat was too high for anyone to afford. This war ended with the capture of Napoleon III at Sedan by a side that consisted of a collection of German states.
question.clue: During this war, Marshal Bazaine retreated his Army of the Rhine from the battle of Gravelotte to the town of Metz.

swap.text: Located on the Jutland peninsula, cities in this state include Flensburg and Lubeck, and is traversed by the Nord-Ostsee Kanal, also known as the Kiel Canal.
swap.clue: John Russell attempted to solve a dispute involving this region by convening the London Conference of 1864, whose annexation violated the earlier London Protocol of 1852.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Otto von Bismarck per part.
question.text: Jesuits and monks were expelled from Prussia, and the May Laws subjugating the Church to the state were issued, in this 1870s campaign against Catholic influence by Bismarck and Adalbert Falk.
question.clue: This social conflict came to an end with the passage of the First Mitigation Law negotiated following the death of Pius IX ], allowing clerics to be exempt from some Prussian laws.

swap.leadin: Name these German politicians of the Cold War.
swap.text: This successor to Walter Ulbricht was the East German leader from 1971 until early 1989, and was so repressive that he even banned Soviet literature as too liberal.
swap.clue: As a result of his terminal cancer, he was allowed to live with his daughter Sonja in instead of standing trial for treason.

question.text: Anti-Nazi theologians like Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Karl Barth formed this Christian movement after the Nazi Party officially absorbed Germany's Protestant church. This movement's views were expressed in the Barmen Declaration.
question.clue: The founding document of this group asserts that the Church is "solely property" of Christ and denies the "false doctrine" that considers it an organ of the State, a position held by the Reichskirche.

swap.leadin: This event saw the downfall of longtime Nazi leader Ernst Rohm.
swap.text: Name this purge perpetrated by the SS and Gestapo to expel the Nazi Party of the SA elite and arrest other political opponents.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Night of the Long Knives</u> [accept <u>Nacht der langen Messer</u>; or <u>Operation</u> <u>Hummingbird</u>]
swap.clue: Among those killed were the socialist Gregor Strasser, former prime minister of Bavaria Gustav von Kahr, and the country's previous chancellor, Kurt von Schleicher.

question.leadin: In 1956, a French protectorate in this region joined West Germany under the Treaty of Luxembourg.
question.text: Identify this coal-rich state in western Germany. A territory in this region was earlier joined to Germany after a 1935 plebiscite.
question.answerHtml: Saarland [accept Saar Protectorate or Territory of the Saar Basin]
question.clue: The Treaty of Versailles made this area an autonmous territory and gave France its coal fields. In a 1935 plebiscite, ninety percent of its voters favored reunion with Germany.

swap.leadin: Passed in the namesake month of 1873, they included the secularization of education, the revocation of political privileges for clergy, and the requirement that all marriages be performed by civil authorities.
swap.text: Name this set of laws designed to restrict Catholic influence on Germany.
swap.clue: One group of laws with this name began a wave of attacks starting in Elizabetgrad and followed from an interpretation of an averted railway accident by Konstantin Pobedonostev.

question.text: This German Field Marshal commanded the winning forces at Sadowa. You may also want to know that he wrote a romance called The Two Friends, which is obviously still highly studied.
question.clue: Some of this commander's success is credited to his troops being armed with the technologically superior "needle gun."

swap.text: Sometimes, Slavic resistance caused rulers like Henry the Lion, a duke of this region, to conquer land violently. Augustus the Strong was Elector of this region before becoming king of Poland.
swap.clue: The first margrave of Brandenburg was a duke of this state named Albert the Bear.

question.leadin: These people, who claimed that they had received messages from the Holy Spirit, were among those labeled as Fanatics by Martin Luther.
question.text: Give this collective name for three religious agitators whose names were probably Nicholas Storch, Thomas Dreschel, and Marcus Stubner.
question.clue: Luther also opposed this group of Anabaptists influenced by Thomas Muntzer. This group, which included Thomas Dreschal and Nicholas Storch, believed themselves to receive messages directly from God.

swap.leadin: During the Thirty Years War, a Spanish campaign gave control over this state to the Catholic Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria, who returned control over its Rhenish territories in the Peace of Westphalia.
swap.text: Name this electoral state in southern Germany that became a center of early Calvinism under a branch of the Wittelsbach dynasty. While ruling this state, Frederick V formed the Protestant Union before the Thirty Years War.
swap.answerHtml: Electoral Palatinate [or the Electorate of the Palatinate; accept Kurpfalz or Kurfürstentum Pfalz]

question.text: This final chancellor of the Weimar Republic tried to invoke Article 48 to purge the Reichstag of extremists, but was largely unable to do so. Hindenberg later relieved him of his chancellorship and appointed Hitler instead.

swap.leadin: This man's forces won a critical victory at the Battle of Tanga, which saw swarms of bees descend on the attackers on the slopes of Kilimanjaro.
swap.text: Name this "Lion of Africa," who led a small band of Askaris and German soldiers on a guerilla campaign against hundreds of thousands of Allied troops before finally surrendering, undefeated, at the end of World War I.
swap.clue: Another member of this family was the final Republican opponent of extending the PATRIOT Act after filling defeating John Conway and Trey Grayson to fill Jim Bunning's Senate seat.
